props.gloss_en: one who lowers walls from above downward: if [the wall] is three tefachim above the ground, [the sukkah] is invalid
from below upward: if [the wall] is ten tefachim high, it is valid
R' Yosei: just as from below upward [it is] ten tefachim, so from above downward [it is] ten tefachim -- a ten-tefach wall lowered from above is valid though it stops three off the ground
the stam: the mishnah's dispute turns on whether a suspended partition permits
one master (R' Yosei) holds: a suspended partition permits
and one master (the sages) holds: a suspended partition does not permit
a cistern between two courtyards: one may not draw from it on Shabbat unless he made it a partition of ten tefachim, whether above, below, or within its rim
Beit Shammai (as RSBG reports, and as the pack's Hebrew reads): [the cistern's partition is made] above -- the Steinsaltz English has the reverse; header
Beit Hillel (as RSBG reports, and as the pack's Hebrew reads): [it is made] below -- the Steinsaltz English has the reverse; header
R' Yehuda: the partition should be no greater than the wall between them -- the courtyards' dividing wall itself permits drawing from the cistern
R' Yehuda said it following R' Yosei's method, who said a suspended partition permits
R' Yehuda said it only there, of eruvei chatzerot, which are rabbinic; but here, sukkah, which is Torah law -- no
R' Yosei said it only here, of sukkah, a positive mitzva; but Shabbat, a prohibition [punished by] stoning -- no
[the Tzippori maaseh was done] not on R' Yosei's authority but on R' Yishmael b. R' Yosei's
Rav Dimi's report: once they forgot to bring a Torah scroll before Shabbat; the next day they SPREAD sheets over the posts, brought the scroll and read from it
rather: they FOUND sheets spread over the posts, brought the scroll and read from it
a mat of four [tefachim] and a bit permits in a sukkah as a wall
the stam: how does he do it? he hangs it in the middle, less than three below and less than three above
and anything less than three is as if joined (lavud)
lest you say: we say one lavud but not two -- he teaches us [that we say two]
the baraita: a mat of seven and a bit permits in a sukkah as a wall
when that [baraita] was taught, it was of a large sukkah
and what does it teach? that walls may be lowered from above downward, as R' Yosei
a board of four and a bit permits in a sukkah as a wall
and he sets it within less than three tefachim of the wall; and anything less than three next to the wall is as if joined
this he teaches: the measure of a small sukkah's extent is seven [tefachim]

objections.gloss_en: ולא היא: neither does R' Yehuda hold like R' Yosei nor R' Yosei like R' Yehuda -- grounds at 16b.4 (p_yehuda_rak_derabanan) and 16b.5 (p_yosei_rak_sukkah). Unanswered: the equation falls.
ואם תאמר: מעשה שנעשה בציפורי, על פי מי נעשה? -- if R' Yosei does not permit a suspended partition on Shabbat, on whose authority was the Tzippori maaseh (16b.7-8) done?

answered_by.gloss_en: לא על פי רבי יוסי, אלא על פי רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי (= p_al_pi_ryishmael)

objections.gloss_en: פירסו סלקא דעתך? מהיכן הביאום בשבת! -- they could not have carried the sheets on Shabbat; replaced by אלא מצאו (p_maaseh_matzu)
מיתיבי: מחצלת שבעה ומשהו מתרת בסוכה משום דופן -- the baraita requires seven and a bit, against Avimi's four and a bit

answered_by.gloss_en: כי תניא ההיא — בסוכה גדולה (= p_baraita_sukkah_gedola)
